command:
set -euo pipefail
cd /tmp

# quast is the independent cross-validator: two assemblers (SPAdes, MEGAHIT) on the
# same fixed reads, one unrelated tool measuring both. We do NOT assert spades==megahit
# (different algorithms legitimately produce different contigs -- like-with-like); we
# assert each assembler's own exact numbers AS QUAST REPORTS THEM. Inputs are the two
# assemblers' staged outputs (this task runs after both -- a resumable S3 chain).
echo "== QUAST evaluates both assemblies =="
quast.py spades_contigs.fasta megahit_contigs.fa -o out -t 2 --labels spades,megahit
cp out/report.tsv report.tsv

# ---- smoke check: parse report.tsv (metric<TAB>spades<TAB>megahit) ----
q() { awk -F'\t' -v k="$1" '$1==k{print $2" "$3}' report.tsv; }
read SC0 MC0 <<< "$(q '# contigs (>= 0 bp)')"   # raw contig counts
read SC MC   <<< "$(q '# contigs')"             # quast default (>=500 bp)
read SN MN   <<< "$(q 'N50')"
read ST MT   <<< "$(q 'Total length')"
{
  echo "spades:  raw_contigs $SC0 want 237 | ge500 $SC want 78 | N50 $SN want 33380 | total $ST want 399846"
  echo "megahit: raw_contigs $MC0 want 2   | ge500 $MC want 1  | N50 $MN want 400429 | total $MT want 400429"
} > smoke-check.txt
cat smoke-check.txt
test "$SC0" -eq 237; test "$SC" -eq 78; test "$SN" -eq 33380; test "$ST" -eq 399846
test "$MC0" -eq 2;   test "$MC" -eq 1;  test "$MN" -eq 400429; test "$MT" -eq 400429
echo "SMOKE CHECK PASSED"
